Purposes & Features

Consent

Cookies, device or similar online identifiers (e.g. login-based identifiers, randomly assigned identifiers, network based identifiers) together with other information (e.g. browser type and information, language, screen size, supported technologies etc.) can be stored or read on your device to recognise it each time it connects to an app or to a website, for one or several of the purposes presented here.

Illustrations

  • Most purposes explained in this notice rely on the storage or accessing of information from your device when you use an app or visit a website. For example, a vendor or publisher might need to store a cookie on your device during your first visit on a website, to be able to recognise your device during your next visits (by accessing this cookie each time).

Legitimate Interest
Consent

Advertising presented to you on this service can be based on limited data, such as the website or app you are using, your non-precise location, your device type or which content you are (or have been) interacting with (for example, to limit the number of times an ad is presented to you).

Illustrations

  • A car manufacturer wants to promote its electric vehicles to environmentally conscious users living in the city after office hours. The advertising is presented on a page with related content (such as an article on climate change actions) after 6:30 p.m. to users whose non-precise location suggests that they are in an urban zone.
  • A large producer of watercolour paints wants to carry out an online advertising campaign for its latest watercolour range, diversifying its audience to reach as many amateur and professional artists as possible and avoiding showing the ad next to mismatched content (for instance, articles about how to paint your house). The number of times that the ad has been presented to you is detected and limited, to avoid presenting it too often.

Consent

Information about your activity on this service (such as forms you submit, content you look at) can be stored and combined with other information about you (for example, information from your previous activity on this service and other websites or apps) or similar users. This is then used to build or improve a profile about you (that might include possible interests and personal aspects). Your profile can be used (also later) to present advertising that appears more relevant based on your possible interests by this and other entities.

Illustrations

  • If you read several articles about the best bike accessories to buy, this information could be used to create a profile about your interest in bike accessories. Such a profile may be used or improved later on, on the same or a different website or app to present you with advertising for a particular bike accessory brand. If you also look at a configurator for a vehicle on a luxury car manufacturer website, this information could be combined with your interest in bikes to refine your profile and make an assumption that you are interested in luxury cycling gear.
  • An apparel company wishes to promote its new line of high-end baby clothes. It gets in touch with an agency that has a network of clients with high income customers (such as high-end supermarkets) and asks the agency to create profiles of young parents or couples who can be assumed to be wealthy and to have a new child, so that these can later be used to present advertising within partner apps based on those profiles.

Consent

Illustrations

  • An online retailer wants to advertise a limited sale on running shoes. It wants to target advertising to users who previously looked at running shoes on its mobile app. Tracking technologies might be used to recognise that you have previously used the mobile app to consult running shoes, in order to present you with the corresponding advertisement on the app.
  • A profile created for personalised advertising in relation to a person having searched for bike accessories on a website can be used to present the relevant advertisement for bike accessories on a mobile app of another organisation.

Consent

  • You are one of very few to have clicked on an advertisement about an “international appreciation day” discount by an online gift shop within the app of a publisher. The publisher wants to have reports to understand how often a specific ad placement within the app, and notably the “international appreciation day” ad, has been viewed or clicked by you and other users, in order to help the publisher and its partners (such as agencies) optimise ad placements.

Taco Bell and Duolingo unite for a worldwide Global Taco Day activation

by Fiona Briggs
October 4, 2026
in Retailer News
Reading Time: 3 mins read
Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 4:35
Instaread

Turns out, “taco” needs no translation. The word remains nearly the same across more than 30 languages, a common thread, all for the love of tacos. Spanish? Taco. French? Taco. German? Taco. Japanese? タコス (Takosu). Hindi? टैको (Taiko).

This Global Taco Day, Tuesday October 6, Taco Bell and Duolingo are putting that universal language to work, taking the annual celebration global for the first time ever and calling on taco fans around the world, including across the UK, to go all out in the name of taco.

Global Taco Day kicks off with an all-new, limited-edition Duo Habanero Sauce, taco-fuelled language fun and plenty of Duo-filled surprises around the world. In the UK, Taco Bell is marking the day by treating the first 150 guests at participating restaurants to a free Crunchy Taco and Duo Habanero Sauce, no purchase necessary, while supplies last.

“Tacos are having a real cultural moment in the UK, and Global Taco Day gives us the perfect excuse to celebrate with our fans,” said Lucy Dee, marketing director, Taco Bell UK & Ireland. “Together with Duolingo, we’re bringing the global idea to life in a way that feels unmistakably Taco Bell – with a free Crunchy Taco, our new Duo Habanero Sauce and a celebration of the one word everyone already knows. No translation required.”

Duo enters his Habanero era

Introducing Duo Habanero Sauce, an all-new, limited-time sauce created exclusively for the Taco Bell x Duolingo collaboration. Bright and tangy with fruity notes and a kick of habanero heat, the sauce delivers a vibrant balance of flavour and spice that builds with every bite. Bold enough to match its namesake, Duo Habanero isn’t one to go unnoticed.

And because no Taco Bell sauce is complete without a little wisdom, Duo Habanero is getting multilingual. In the UK, the limited-edition sauce ramekins feature taco-inspired wisdoms across English, French, Spanish and German, which are some of the top languages Brits are learning on Duolingo. Every wisdom is a reminder that while languages may differ, the love of tacos is universal.

“Language and food are two of the most powerful ways we connect with culture and with each other,” said Emmanuel Orssaud, chief marketing officer, Duolingo. “Taco is a rare word that travels easily across cultures, making it a fun starting point for getting people curious about language.”

Across participating markets globally, Taco Bell and Duolingo are bringing Global Taco Day to life with local offers, activations and limited-edition surprises inspired by the universal love of tacos.

The UK speaks taco

Taco Bell and Duolingo are giving UK fans even more ways to get in on the action, with limited-edition swag and chances to unlock a little more Duolingo.

On Tuesday, October 6, 50 limited-edition Taco Bell x Duolingo plushies will be up for grabs exclusively through Live Más Club. Fans simply need to open the Taco Bell UK app before 11 a.m., head to Live Más Club and be one of the first 50 to claim.

Fans will also have the chance to score one of 5,000 Duolingo Super codes, each unlocking one month free of Duolingo Super. Additional details on when and how to claim will be announced soon on Taco Bell UK’s social channels.

The UK celebration is part of a wider Global Taco Day programme taking place around the world, with local offers and activations bringing Taco Bell and Duolingo’s shared celebration of taco culture to fans in participating markets.

For the love of taco fans

Taco Bell has a history of making more of National Taco Day. In 2023, Taco Bell helped liberate “Taco Tuesday” in the United States, opening the phrase up for restaurants nationwide. Then, in 2024, Taco Bell took on the calendar itself, working with National Day Calendar to move National Taco Day to the first Tuesday in October. The brand celebrated the newly minted National Taco Day first anniversary in 2025 with special deals for fans.

The trademark? Cancelled. The calendar? Fixed. Next up: going global. With Duolingo along for the ride, it’s the next notch in Taco Bell’s years-long effort to make the day bigger for taco fans everywhere.

“We’ve always believed tacos are for everyone,” said Amy Ellis Durini, Chief Marketing and Strategy Officer, Taco Bell International. “There’s something pretty special about a word that can be understood across languages and cultures. Together with Duolingo, we’re celebrating a love of tacos that brings people together everywhere – and the idea that sometimes the things that connect us need very little translation at all.”

Rituals arrives in Leicester Fosse Park, marking its 150th store

by Fiona Briggs
October 3, 2026
in Retailer News
Reading Time: 2 mins read

It’s often the smallest rituals that make a day: the unhurried shower after a long one, the scent that tells you you’re home. Rituals is bringing more of those moments to Leicester as it opens its 150th store at Fosse Park, built on the belief that a small act can change the shape of your whole day.

Spanning 168m2, the new store is an invitation to slow down and take a moment, whether for yourself or for someone you love. Shoppers will find luxury perfume and skincare, indulgent bath and body favourites and fragrances for the home, all created to turn the simplest routines into something more meaningful.

Leicester Fosse Park joins a growing Rituals family present in 33 countries, from Paris and Hong Kong to London, and becomes the brand’s 150th store in the UK.

To mark the occasion, Rituals has a few thoughtful extras in store:

Saturday 3rd October: the offer returns, with 25% off Shower Foams and a gift with purchase on spends of £45 or more.

Also on Saturday:

The first 50 customers to spend £35 or more will also receive a Rituals goodie bag.
A photobooth will be live in store from 11am to 3pm, so customers can capture the moment.

“Reaching our 150th store is a moment we’re incredibly proud of, and there’s no better place to celebrate this milestone than Leicester. Care sits at the heart of everything we do, and we hope our new Fosse Park store becomes a place where customers can pause, treat themselves, or find something special for someone they love. For us, it’s always the small things that make life feel a little more special,” said Annemarie Forsyth, managing director, Rituals UK and IE.

From a moment of self-care to a thoughtful gift for someone you love, the Rituals team at Fosse Park is ready to welcome Leicester through the doors.

Rituals Cosmetics Leicester Fosse Park, Unit 11, Fosse Park Shopping Centre, Fosse Park Avenue, Leicester, Leicestershire, LE19 1HX
